subject.title: [Bug]: Sandbox container exits immediately when no-new-privileges is applied (exec /usr/bin/sleep: operation not permitted)

question: Should OpenClaw support a Docker sandbox `no-new-privileges` opt-out or fallback for hosts where that Docker flag makes sandbox startup fail with `operation not permitted`?
rationale: The source-reproducible failure blocks sandbox sessions, but disabling or retrying without this flag changes the sandbox hardening boundary and adds config/fallback behavior that requires maintainer security/product judgment.

options.title: Explicit Dangerous Override
options.body: Add a documented `sandbox.docker` opt-out that defaults to the current secure behavior and reports weakened sandboxes in status, doctor, and dangerous-config output.

options.title: Diagnostic Only
options.body: Keep `no-new-privileges` mandatory and improve startup/status errors so operators can identify the host-level Docker incompatibility without patching dist files blindly.

options.title: Narrow EPERM Fallback
options.body: Retry without the flag only for a tightly detected startup EPERM and record the runtime as weakened for audit/status visibility.

recommendation.title: Explicit Dangerous Override
recommendation.body: Add a documented `sandbox.docker` opt-out that defaults to the current secure behavior and reports weakened sandboxes in status, doctor, and dangerous-config output.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the clearest history signal for the introduced Docker sandbox module containing the hardening flag.
